about: Named places to eat and fun things to do in and near Paramaribo, for Bunny Goes. Same item fields as site.json, plus area, address, hours and tags. Facts come from search results with source URLs; the research proxy blocked opening most pages, so check hours before going.

items.label: Roti Shop Joosje (Zwartenhovenbrugstraat)
items.fun: Thick, soft roti that has been rolled here since 1942. Your first proper Parbo lunch.
items.value: Long-running roti shop in the city centre, described by travel guides as making roti since 1942. KLM's guide gives the address as Zwartenhovenbrugstraat 9. Reviewers praise the thick roti bread and the chicken, potato and greens roti as filling for the price, mention friendly, patient staff (one helped a diner who did not speak Dutch), air-conditioned indoor seating and very clean toilets. Some found portions small and the interior a bit plain.
items.notes: Lunch spot; air-conditioning makes it a good midday escape from the heat.

sources.publisher: KLM travel guide (Paramaribo, a culinary melting pot)
Wanderlog (Roti Shop Joosje listing with reviews)

items.limits: No dated 2025-2026 review seen directly; hours and prices not found in any source. Generic Joosje item exists elsewhere in the guide.

items.label: Roopram Roti (Grote Hofstraat / Watermolenstraat)
items.fun: Ten-plus kinds of roti, from chicken to egg to liver. Pick a new one every week.
items.value: Roopram is a Surinamese roti chain that, per KLM, sells more than 10 types of roti including chicken, egg and liver. A 2017 travel blog places the branch nearest the Waterkant at the corner of Watermolenstraat and Grote Hofstraat, near the Post Office, and says the chain has several locations in the city. Wanderlog reviews are mixed: some praise the rotis, others complain of little filling for the price.
items.notes: Check Google Maps for the nearest branch; the corner location is from a 2017 source.
items.address: Corner of Watermolenstraat and Grote Hofstraat (2017 source)

sources.publisher: KLM travel guide (Paramaribo, a culinary melting pot)
Concrete and Kitsch (travel blog, Food in Suriname: roti)

items.limits: Branch address is from a 2017 blog and could have changed; no current Paramaribo hours found (hours online are for Dutch branches). Generic Roopram item exists elsewhere.

items.label: Martin's House of Indian Food (Rainville)
items.fun: Home-cooked Indian from a huge menu, worth the short taxi ride out of town.
items.value: Indian restaurant in the residential Rainville neighbourhood. Lonely Planet describes tasty home-cooked Indian food from a voluminous menu and says it is well worth the short taxi ride from the centre.
items.notes: Take a taxi; it is outside the centre in a residential area.

sources.publisher: Lonely Planet (Must-see restaurants in Suriname, mirror copy)

items.limits: Single guidebook source (via a mirror copy), undated; could not confirm it is still open in 2026, nor address, hours or prices.

items.label: Restaurant Sarinah (Verlengde Gemenelandsweg)
items.fun: Indonesian feast territory: rendang, nasi rames and, if you are lucky, a whole rijsttafel.
items.value: Well-known Indonesian/Javanese restaurant south of the centre at Verlengde Gemenelandsweg 187 (per iExplore), which calls it the best Indonesian food in town and lists rijsttafel among its signature dishes. Wanderlog lists rendang, nasi rames and Bami Sarinah, generous portions, affordable prices, friendly staff and a takeaway counter; service can be slow.
items.notes: Go with time to spare as service can be slow; takeaway is an option.

sources.publisher: Wanderlog (50 best restaurants in Paramaribo list)

items.limits: Rijsttafel only confirmed by one undated guide; ask whether it needs booking or a minimum party size. Hours not found.

items.label: Mirosso (Blauwgrond)
items.fun: The neat, pretty warung of Blauwgrond. Saoto, satay and pandan dawet to finish.
items.value: Javanese-Surinamese restaurant in Blauwgrond, noted by Wanderlog for its elegant, immaculate Indonesian-style interior with air-conditioned indoor and outdoor seating. Most praised: saoto soup and satay; reviewers also mention spicy coconut beef, pandan dawet, homemade ketjap and tamarind juice. Some found prices slightly high, others call it one of the best meals of their trip.
items.notes: A gentle first warung: tidier and calmer than the street stalls. Go by taxi in the evening.
items.limits: One aggregator source; street address, hours and prices not found. Could not confirm 2026 status independently.

items.label: Warung Felicia (Blauwgrond)
items.fun: Honest, cheap nasi and bami, plus a late-night saoto when you need a hug in a bowl.
items.value: Blauwgrond warung described as offering honest and affordable Indonesian food. Reviewers single out the nasi and bami, and one recommends the saoto as a good late-night choice.
items.notes: Small family warung; bring cash and take a taxi home at night.
items.limits: Single aggregator source; no address or hours found. Cash-only is a general warung assumption, not stated by the source.

items.label: Warung Renah (Paramaribo)
items.fun: A reviewer swears the saoto tastes like real Surinamese-Javanese home cooking.
items.value: Javanese warung listed on Tripadvisor in Paramaribo; a reviewer recommends its saoto and says the food tastes like real Surinamese-Javanese cooking. It also appears in Trip.com's Paramaribo restaurant lists without reviews.
items.limits: Thin evidence; neighbourhood, address, hours and recent reviews not found.

items.label: Blauwgrond warungs (evening Javanese food street)
items.fun: Paramaribo's Javanese food heartland: hop between warungs for saoto, satay and bami.
items.value: Blauwgrond began as a Javanese village north of the centre and is now known mainly as Suriname's Javanese culinary centre, with many warungs and restaurants. KLM describes the warungs as authentic eateries that are often an extension of a home. Guided evening city tours include a stop at the Blauwgrond warungs (food not included in the tour price).
items.notes: Best in the evening; it is not walkable from the centre, so go by taxi or with an evening tour the first time.

sources.publisher: KLM travel guide (Paramaribo, a culinary melting pot)
Musement (Paramaribo three-hour evening guided tour listing)

items.limits: Area item, not one business; individual warungs open and close often. Named options: Mirosso, Warung Felicia.

conflicts: Lonely Planet describes Creole food; Wanderlog's description emphasises Javanese/Indonesian dishes.
A second Evendo listing gives Verlengde Gemenelandsweg 139 for a De Gadri; may be another branch or an error.
items.label: De Gadri (Zeelandiaweg, by Fort Zeelandia)
items.fun: Lunch on a breezy patio beside the fort and the river, with a plate of pom.
items.value: Casual outdoor restaurant next to Fort Zeelandia and the Suriname River. Lonely Planet calls it a quiet spot with Parbo's best Creole food; reviewers mention Surinamese dishes such as pom, while Wanderlog's description lists Javanese/Indonesian dishes. Reviewers say it is a very popular lunch spot with tourists and locals. Evendo lists Zeelandiaweg 1 and hours of 8:00 to 19:00 daily.
items.notes: A lunch place, not a late dinner: a Reddit user notes it does not stay open late.

sources.publisher: Lonely Planet (Must-see restaurants in Suriname, mirror copy)

items.limits: Hours from one aggregator, undated.

conflicts: One listing labels the address area 'Rainville' although Costerstraat is in the old centre.
items.label: Souposo (Costerstraat)
items.fun: Peanut soup and homemade sorrel juice in a leafy backyard full of birdsong.
items.value: Soup-focused restaurant at Costerstraat 20 with a shaded backyard patio. Reviewers most often praise the peanut soup (especially with the homemade hibiscus juice), cassava soup and tom tom (plantain dumplings); Lonely Planet cites delicious daily soups and mains. Staff are described as friendly and quick, though one reviewer found the satay salty. Listings show about 4.1 to 4.2 out of 5 across several hundred reviews; one lists weekday hours of 9:00 to 21:00.
items.notes: Lovely for a solo lunch with a book; smoking nearby on the patio was one complaint.

sources.publisher: Lonely Planet (Must-see restaurants in Suriname, mirror copy)

items.limits: Weekend hours not found;

items.label: Amaranta (Creole restaurant)
items.fun: Cassava soup, fried fish with pineapple and a pepper sauce people write home about.
items.value: Creole restaurant recommended by Caribbean Beat as one of the good Creole places in town. Its example lunch: cassava soup, then fried fish with pineapple, brown beans and white rice; the writer praises the pepper sauce as some of the tastiest they had.
items.limits: Single magazine source of uncertain (likely older) date; address, hours and 2026 status not confirmed.

items.label: Krioro (breakfast, centre)
items.fun: Start the day with a pom broodje in flaky bread from a board full of fillings.
items.value: Popular breakfast spot in the city centre, per Caribbean Beat, with a menu board of fillings for bread rolls. The writer's pick is pom in a freshly baked roll.
items.limits: Single older magazine source; address, hours and 2026 status not confirmed.

items.label: Chi Min (Cornelis Jongbawstraat)
items.fun: Cooked-to-order noodles and spicy chicken. Very much a taste of a Chinese canteen.
items.value: Chinese restaurant at Cornelis Jongbawstraat 83, phone +597 412-155. Frommer's recommends its cooked-to-order noodles; reviewers mention a spicy chicken dish and Singapore mi foen with shrimp, generous portions, reasonable prices and friendly staff, though food can take a long time. Takeaway downstairs, dining upstairs.
items.notes: Allow time; several reviewers say dishes are slow to arrive.
items.limits: Hours not found; small review count on Trip.com.

items.label: Dumpling No. 1
items.fun: Big steamed or fried dumplings, exactly as the name promises. Dumpling cravings, solved.
items.value: Chinese spot recommended by Caribbean Beat as doing exactly what it says: sizeable steamed or fried dumplings with meat or vegetable fillings, plus stir-fried noodles with pork and greens as a chef's special. A personal blog also mentions it satisfying a dim sum craving.

sources.publisher: Annie Paul (personal blog post on Paramaribo)

items.limits: Older sources only; the per-dumpling price quoted by Caribbean Beat is long out of date so not used. Address, hours and 2026 status not confirmed.

items.label: Garden of Eden (Virolastraat, Thai)
items.fun: Thai food in a serene garden. Dress up a little; this is a special-occasion place.
items.value: Thai restaurant on Virolastraat, phone +597 499448, described by Wanderlog as known for its harmonious interior and garden setting, with Thai chefs and vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. Reviewers mention a formal side and a cosy noodle bar. A Reddit user calls it one of the best restaurants in Suriname; reviewers say it costs a bit more than average but is worth it. Trip.com shows it opening at 18:00.
items.notes: Dinner only (opens 18:00 per Trip.com); book for a birthday or a treat night.
items.limits: Area 'Zorg en Hoop' is my placement of Virolastraat and was not stated in sources; some reviewers note uneven service.

items.label: Baka Foto (inside Fort Zeelandia)
items.fun: Coffee and salads by day, a candlelit river-view dinner by night inside an old fort.
items.value: Restaurant inside Fort Zeelandia. KLM's guide says it serves coffee, sandwiches and salads by day and dinner with a view over the Suriname River at night, mixing international cooking with Surinamese influences, for example pom with duck and orange, or local tuna prepared four ways.
items.notes: Combine with a fort visit; take a taxi home after dark.

sources.publisher: KLM travel guide (Old Fort Zeelandia in Paramaribo)

items.limits: Single undated source; hours, prices and 2026 status not confirmed.

conflicts: Wanderlog lists a 'Roline's de Waag' at the same Waterkant 5 address; may be a different operator or a predecessor.
items.label: Bodega & Grill De Waag (Waterkant 5)
items.fun: A stylish grill in an old riverside weigh-house, right on the Waterkant.
items.value: Western-style grill restaurant in the historic Waag building at Waterkant 5. Lonely Planet describes an old waterfront building transformed into a smart, stylish space. iExplore calls De Waag at the same address the best breakfast spot in the city. Trip.com lists phone +31 6 36415439 (a Dutch number) and average spend estimates of roughly NZD 41 per person.
items.notes: Central and on the river, easy to reach by taxi in the evening.

sources.publisher: Lonely Planet (Must-see restaurants in Suriname, mirror copy)
Trip.com (Bodega and Grill De Waag listing)

items.limits: Hours not found; price estimates on Trip.com differ by regional page so not used.

items.label: Sushi-Ya (Henck Arronstraat 63)
items.fun: Japanese chefs, a sushi counter and a crunchy roll with your name on it.
items.value: Japanese restaurant at Henck Arronstraat 63, phone +597 475450, with table seating and a counter. Lonely Planet says Japanese chefs make excellent sushi; a Wanderlog reviewer recommends the Crunchy Roll, Alaska Roll and fish katsu. Reviews note no air-conditioning and slow service. Trip.com shows it opening at 18:00; Courtyard by Marriott lists it as a nearby Japanese open-terrace restaurant.
items.notes: Reserve ahead and dress for warm evenings: it is open-air.

sources.publisher: Lonely Planet (Must-see restaurants in Suriname, mirror copy)
Courtyard by Marriott Paramaribo (official hotel dining page)

items.limits: Hours from one snapshot; prices not found.

items.label: Mingle Paramaribo (International Mall of Suriname)
items.fun: Sushi, filet mignon and cocktails in a buzzy mall lounge. Shop first, then eat.
items.value: Lively lounge-restaurant inside the International Mall of Suriname, with a menu including filet mignon, California rolls and sushi. Reviewers praise service, food, ambience and prices, though one found it overpriced. Wanderlog advises booking ahead on weekends and arriving before 20:00 if you want to shop, as mall shops close at 21:00.
items.notes: Book on weekends. A mall setting feels easy and safe for a solo evening.
items.limits: Single aggregator source; Area 'Zuid' for the mall is my placement, not stated by the source.

items.label: Lee's Korean Restaurant (Mahonylaan)
items.fun: Korean comfort food in town. Bibimbap nights when you miss Asian flavours.
items.value: Korean/Asian restaurant at Mahonylaan 12-14, phone +597 479834. Listed hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 11:00-15:00 and 18:00-22:00, closed Sunday and Monday (Pearl); Trip.com shows similar lunch and dinner windows (11:00-15:30, 18:00-22:30).
items.notes: Closed Sundays and Mondays.
items.limits: Price is a crowd-sourced Trip.com average, not a menu price; hours differ slightly between sources.

items.label: Het Pannekoek & Poffertjes Cafe (Van Sommelsdijckstraat 11)
items.fun: Dutch pancakes and tiny poffertjes a block from the river. Sweet, cosy, very cute.
items.value: Cafe at Van Sommelsdijckstraat 11, a block off Kleine Waterstraat, phone +597 422-914. Wanderlog says it serves Dutch-style pancakes alongside Surinamese dishes (such as cassava with codfish) and Angus steak. Reviewers praise breakfast, espresso and prices; complaints are a Dutch/French-only menu and uneven service.
items.notes: Good breakfast or sweet treat near the hotel strip; have a translation app ready for the menu.
items.limits: Hours and prices not found; no dated recent review seen.

items.label: Mighty Racks (Van Sommelsdijckstraat 18)
items.fun: Ribs, wings and a burger called the boyfriend's bang bang. Bring an appetite.
items.value: Grill restaurant at Van Sommelsdijckstraat 18, phone +597 520458. Listings highlight grilled ribs, burgers (the 'boyfriends bang bang burger'), local filet mignon and big portions. Some diners say meals were not served hot and staff reviews are mixed.
items.notes: Evening spot in the walkable Kleine Waterstraat area.
items.limits: Hours differ between listings (Trip.com once showed 16:00 to midnight).

items.label: The Rooftop Restaurant & Bar (Kleine Waterstraat 9)
items.fun: Sunset dinner up high over the Torarica strip. Your dress-up, treat-yourself night.
items.value: Rooftop restaurant and bar at Kleine Waterstraat 9, listed by TableAgent as fine dining with reservations recommended and casual dress, tagged for romantic dining and dining alone. Ogi Sushi & Teppanyaki is listed at the same address. Both carry a $$ price tier.
items.notes: Book ahead; good choice for a solo treat as it is tagged for dining alone and sits in the busy hotel zone.
items.limits: Directory listings only; no menu, hours or dated reviews found.

items.label: Las Tias (Johannes Mungrastraat 75)
items.fun: Latin-Cuban fusion, good cocktails and quesadillas for a girls' night out.
items.value: Latin/Cuban fusion restaurant at Johannes Mungrastraat 75, phone +597 434-162. Dishes listed include spicy chicken and shrimp pasta, quesadillas and wonton soup. Diners often praise service and cocktails; others found the food bland or overpriced. Trip.com showed it opening at 07:30.
items.limits: Mixed reviews; full hours and prices not found.

items.label: Hard Rock Cafe Suriname (International Mall of Suriname)
items.fun: Burgers and rock memorabilia in the city's shiniest mall. Familiar, easy, no surprises.
items.value: Official Hard Rock Cafe inside the International Mall of Suriname, which Hard Rock calls the country's most modern mall; over 5,250 sq ft with seating for up to 144 guests. There is also a Hard Rock at the airport.
items.notes: A safe, predictable fallback on an anxious day; check the official page for hours.
items.limits: Hours not captured from the official page; area 'Zuid' is my placement of the mall.

items.label: Coffee Mama (Costerstraat, Centrum)
items.fun: A cosy little Caribbean coffee nook that guesthouse guests call the best cup in town.
items.value: Coffee Mama is a small coffee bar serving premium coffee and Caribbean bites in a cosy Caribbean-style setting. Address: Costerstraat 62, Paramaribo (historic centre, a few doors from Couleur Locale guesthouse). Wanderlog and the Destinito guide give hours of Monday to Saturday about 8:00 to 21:00, closed Sunday, and mention an outdoor terrace. It has active Facebook and Instagram pages (@coffeemama.paramaribo).
items.notes: Easy walk from the Waterkant and Cathedral, so a good first-week treat. Closed Sundays.
items.limits: Price range is Tripadvisor's band, not a menu. Hours from aggregators; confirm on Facebook.
conflicts: Phone numbers differ: Facebook +597 895-9961, Destinito 726-0753 and 894-9896.

items.label: The Sweetest Thing (dessert cafe)
items.fun: Passionfruit cheesecake and brownies people call the best they've ever had. Go on.
items.value: Small, cosy dessert spot known for homemade cakes: reviewers single out passionfruit and Oreo cheesecake, brownies, Dutch apple pie and homemade cookies, with espresso and tea. food 4.9). Wanderlog notes a small room with only a couple of tables. Tripadvisor, Foursquare and MapQuest give Johan Adolf Pengelstraat 112-114; Suriname Hub lists Tweede Rijweg 94.
items.notes: Space is tiny, so go mid-afternoon on a weekday. Check the address before you set off.
items.limits: Small review base and some reviews are several years old; one reviewer complained of slow service. Could not confirm it is open in late 2026 or which address is current. No hours found.
conflicts: Address: J.A. Pengelstraat 112-114 (Tripadvisor, Foursquare, MapQuest) vs Tweede Rijweg 94 (Suriname Hub, ~2025).

items.label: C&Y Coffee + Roasters (Gompertstraat, Noord)
items.fun: A proper roaster with cakes by day and a little bistro buzz at night.
items.value: Coffee roaster and cafe serving coffee, breakfast breads, savoury snacks and cakes, with an evening bistro offer (Suriname4you). Address: Jacques Gompertstraat 38, corner of Plutostraat, Paramaribo. Listings give hours of roughly Tuesday to Thursday 9:30-22:00, Friday to Sunday 9:30-23:00 and Monday from about 16:00. Phone +597 550-661. a Wanderlog reviewer calls it an excellent coffee spot for meeting friends.
items.notes: Gompertstraat is a lively strip of cafes and boba shops, good for a weekend wander. Take a taxi from the centre.
items.limits: Hours vary between listings; an older Tripadvisor entry says 9:00-23:00 daily. Tripadvisor review count not captured.
conflicts: Hours: aggregators list a late Monday opening; older Tripadvisor says 9:00-23:00 daily.

items.label: The Coffee Box (Lalla Rookhweg / Noord)
items.fun: Giant frappes in mason jars and a big terrace for a lazy weekend brunch.
items.value: Casual coffee shop with quesadillas, frappes, wings, cocktails and appetisers (Wanderlog). Reviewers love the large frappes served in mason jars, including an Oreo marshmallow frappe. Tripadvisor and Wanderlog give Lalla Rookhweg 22/22A; Explore Suriname lists two locations including Wilhelminastraat 66-68. The Reismonkey blog (2025-26) recommends the Paramaribo Noord branch for its big terrace and says it is popular for weekend breakfast and brunch.
items.notes: Weekend mornings get busy. The Lalla Rookhweg branch is near Hermitage Mall, so you can pair it with shopping.
items.limits: Branch addresses are muddled across listings; hours not found. Confirm which branch you are heading to.
conflicts: Explore Suriname lists Wilhelminastraat 66-68 with a different phone number; others list Lalla Rookhweg 22/22A.

items.label: Bella Italia gelato (Van Sommelsdijckstraat)
items.fun: Cotton candy, bubble gum or whiskey cake gelato? Pick three, nobody's judging.
items.value: Italian-style gelato shop at Van Sommelsdijckstraat 8 in the tourist area, with fresh daily gelato (per its Instagram), playful flavours from bubble gum and cotton candy to whiskey cake, plus banana splits and crepes. Featured in Suriname Hub's '3 Ice Cream Shops in Paramaribo'. Phone 520-200 on its social pages. Active Facebook (page created 2024), Instagram and TikTok presence.
items.notes: Perfect after an evening stroll along the Waterkant. Hours seen only in a TikTok post (11:00-23:00).
items.limits: No prices or verified hours.

items.label: Padre Nostro (Koninginnestraat) for homemade gelato
items.fun: An Italian restaurant whose homemade gelato uses local fruits like acai. Dessert first?
items.value: Italian restaurant at Koninginnestraat 11 in the centre, known for its homemade gelato: Suriname Hub says it has made gelato since 2016 and now produces more than 30 flavours, mostly water-based. Tripadvisor reviewers recommend flavours using local fruit such as acai, and rum raisin. Phone +597 864-9163. Accepts cards; one review says USD and SRD are accepted.
items.notes: Evening place (one listing shows 17:00-22:00), so pair gelato with a pasta dinner. Taxi home at night.
items.limits: Hours from one possibly outdated listing. Mainly a restaurant, not a walk-in ice cream counter. The 'since 2016, 30+ flavours' detail came via a search summary of the Suriname Hub ice cream article.

items.label: Alegria ice cream (Keizerstraat, since 1983)
items.fun: Paramaribo's old-school ice cream and cupcake shop, scooping since 1983.
items.value: Classic ice cream parlour in the city centre, part of Paramaribo's ice cream scene since 1983 (Suriname Hub). Facebook gives Keizerstraat 49 with hours 9:00-22:00, Sundays and holidays 15:00-22:00; phone +597 472-785. A newer 'Alegria South' branch is listed at Johannes Mungrastraat 68 (Social Suriname, updated January 2026).
items.notes: Go in the afternoon heat. Sunday opening is later (15:00).
items.limits: Tripadvisor reviews are old (newest seen 2015). Could not confirm the Keizerstraat shop is still trading in 2026; the South branch listing is the most recent evidence.

items.label: Sabores da Amazonia / Amazonia Ice Cream (IMS mall)
items.fun: Brazilian artisan ice cream in acai, cupuacu and awara. Taste the rainforest.
items.value: Artisanal ice cream with Amazonian ingredients such as cupuacu, acai, bacuri and awara, made without preservatives (per its Facebook). Located in the International Mall of Suriname (IMS), Unit H3, Ringweg-Zuid 245. The official IMS store page gives Monday-Saturday 14:00-21:00 and Sunday 16:00-21:00; phone (+597) 893-2844.
items.notes: IMS is air-conditioned and has plenty of food options, a safe easy outing by taxi.
items.address: International Mall of Suriname, Unit H3, Ringweg-Zuid 245

sources.publisher: International Mall of Suriname (official store page)

items.limits: Hours differ on MallsByCountry (15:00-22:30).
conflicts: Hours: IMS site 14-21 (Sun 16-21) vs MallsByCountry 15:00-22:30.
Address number 245 (IMS) vs 243 (Facebook).

items.label: SIP TEA bubble tea (Jodenbreestraat and branches)
items.fun: Your boba fix: HK-style, Thai and matcha milk tea, right in the centre.
items.value: Suriname-based bubble tea chain. Centrum branch at Jodenbreestraat 43; other branches listed on Instagram at Kasabaholoweg 121, Zinniastraat 25 and Midtown Mall Lelydorp. Signature milk teas include HK Style, Classic, Assam, Thai Tea and Matcha. Active Facebook and Instagram (@siptea.suriname).
items.notes: The Kasabaholo branch posted a temporary closure (23 Sept to 12 Nov); check posts before going.
items.limits: Only the shop's own pages; no independent reviews, hours or prices found. Year of the Kasabaholo closure notice not confirmed.

items.label: JellyBubbles (Lindastraat and Gompertstraat)
items.fun: Bubble tea with jelly, slushes and milkshakes: a drink that's fun to eat.
items.value: Bubble tea shop selling bubble teas, smoothies, milkshakes and slushes with jelly and tapioca toppings. South branch at Lindastraat 1 (corner Johannes Mungrastraat), phone 439689; North branch at J. Gompertstraat 115, phone 457908 (per its Instagram/Facebook). Also on the Bestel.sr delivery platform. Mapcarta lists Mon-Sat 11:00-20:00, Sun 15:00-20:00.
items.notes: Can be ordered via Bestel.sr if you are not up for going out.
items.limits: No independent reviews or prices. Hours differ between Mapcarta and Waze.
conflicts: Sunday hours: Mapcarta 15:00-20:00 vs Waze 12:00-17:30.

items.label: Petit Bouchon (French bakery above 't Vat)
items.fun: Croissants by a French baker and a weekend brunch upstairs. Tres jolie.
items.value: Described on its Facebook page as Suriname's first artisan bakery and pastry shop, run by a French baker. First floor at Kleine Waterstraat 1 (above 't Vat), phone +597 715-1545. Serves a homemade brunch on weekends 10:00-14:00. Social Suriname also lists it as an artisanal bakery and pastry shop.
items.notes: Weekend brunch is the thing; then wander to the Waterkant and Fort Zeelandia nearby.
items.hours: Weekend brunch 10:00-14:00 (Facebook); other hours not found
items.limits: Facebook page appears new (2025); only two reviews on a ranking site. Weekday hours unknown.

items.label: Jage Caffe (Gompertstraat and IMS)
items.fun: Specialty espresso and Nutella pancakes in a small, buzzy brunch spot.
items.value: Small specialty-coffee brunch cafe at Gompertstraat 118 (next to Sash Fashion), with a second branch, Jage Caffe 2.0, at IMS mall Unit G1. Destinito recommends scrambled eggs with salmon, American pancakes and Nutella pancakes, and warns tables fill fast on weekend mornings. Phone +597 712-5412. Reismonkey also recommends it.
items.notes: Go before 10:00 at weekends or on a weekday. Possibly closed Mondays.
items.hours: Conflicting: Mon-Sat 8:00-16:00 (Instagram) or Tue-Fri 9:00-18:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-18:00, Mon closed (Destinito)
items.limits: Hours conflict between sources. No prices found.
conflicts: Hours: Instagram Mon-Sat 8-16 vs Destinito Tue-Fri 9-18, weekends 10-18, Mon closed.

items.label: SHLX Cafe (Verlengde Gemenelandsweg)
items.fun: A cosy, pretty spot for breakfast, brunch and lunch with the girls (or just you).
items.value: Breakfast, brunch and lunch cafe at Verlengde Gemenelandsweg 164, phone +597 746 0933, linked to the SHLX Collection shop. Social Suriname featured it in March 2025 as a cosy breakfast, brunch and lunch spot. Instagram hours: Mon-Fri 8:00-17:30, Sat-Sun 9:00-15:00.
items.notes: Daytime only. Same road as Shafantur Mall, so combine with Maillard or Sundae Bliss.
conflicts: Facebook gives Mon-Sat 8:00-16:30; Instagram gives weekday and weekend hours as listed.

items.label: The Maillard Cafe (Shafantur Mall)
items.fun: Artisan pastries and specialty drinks in a polished little patisserie. Very you.
items.value: Cafe and patisserie serving artisan pastries, specialty coffee and brunch. Instagram lists Gemenelandsweg 147, Shafantur Mall unit 101, plus a second spot inside Choi's Supermarket. Phone 897-3355 on one listing. Covered by Destinito as a specialty coffee and brunch spot and listed on Suriname Hub and Explore Suriname.
items.notes: Not to be confused with the Maillard Cafe in Malolos, Philippines.
conflicts: Street number: 147 (Instagram, listing) vs #164 (TikTok) vs 168 (Mapcarta).

items.label: Rituals Coffee House (Hotel Krasnapolsky)
items.fun: Chain-style comfort: lattes, smoothies, bagels and cake on a central terrace.
items.value: Coffee house franchise (originally from Trinidad and Tobago) on the ground floor of Hotel Krasnapolsky, Domineestraat 39, in the shopping heart of the centre. Menu covers coffee, tea, smoothies, cakes, bagels, sandwiches and daily soup, with a terrace. Cityzapper's coffee-and-lunch guide lists it among the city's best coffee spots. The closest thing to a Starbucks-style chain cafe found in Paramaribo.
items.notes: Handy, air-conditioned meeting point on Domineestraat, near Readytex and the Waterkant.

sources.publisher: This Girl Can Cook (Dutch food blog)

items.limits: Hotel and Rituals listings are several years old; hours not found. Phone numbers differ between sources.

items.label: Tasty Fresh Food & Coffee Bar (Kirpalani, Pengelstraat)
items.fun: Coffee and a chipotle chicken melt after a Kirpalani shopping spree.
items.value: American-style cafe for coffee, breakfast and sandwiches inside the Kirpalani Superstore at J.A. Pengelstraat 163 (Kirpalani says 3rd floor), phone +597 402-797. Open seven days a week on the store's schedule. reviewers praise the sandwiches. Kirpalani lists other Tasty branches at Domineestraat 52-56, Koningstraat 14A and Maagdenstraat 19-27.
items.notes: Good rainy-day stop: shop, then coffee, all indoors.
items.hours: Daily, same hours as Kirpalani Superstore (official)
items.limits: Exact hours not stated; a dated directory gave Mon-Sat 8:00-19:30, Sun 12:00-19:30. Review count not captured.
conflicts: Floor: 3rd (Kirpalani, Tripadvisor) vs 2nd (one directory).

items.label: Sara's Brunch Cafe (Johannes Mungrastraat)
items.fun: Garden seating, free wifi and a budget-friendly brunch. Bring a book.
items.value: Small breakfast and brunch spot with garden seating at Johannes Mungrastraat 23, phone +597 433-347. Menu includes sandwiches, local dishes such as pepperpot, pasta, soups, fish in ginger sauce and battered shrimp. Tripadvisor 4.2 from about 11 reviews, budget price range; free wifi. Suriname Hub lists weekday hours from 8:00 to 15:30.
items.notes: Daytime only. Service can be a bit slow.
items.hours: Mon-Fri approx. 8:00-15:30 (Suriname Hub); Saturday listed too
items.limits: Small review base. Hours partial; confirm on Facebook.

items.label: Combe Bazaar (Wilhelminastraat)
items.fun: The local breakfast ritual: a fat Surinamese broodje with bakkeljauw or pom.
items.value: Morning-only sandwich shop at Wilhelminastraat 23 known for Surinamese broodjes with bakkeljauw (salt fish), pom, zoutvlees, curry egg, tempeh or liver, plus coffee, juices and soup. Reismonkey calls it the ideal spot for breakfast or an early lunch. A Tripadvisor reviewer quoted about 90 SRD for a standard broodje with Surinamese filling. Phone +597 424-648.
items.notes: Go early: it is a morning place (an older listing says 7:00-13:00). Cash is safest.
items.limits: Price from one review of uncertain date. Hours from a 2020 listing. Some reviews say fillings can be salty.

items.label: Cafe Bibis (by Passionate Cakes & Snacks Designs)
items.fun: A hidden weekday gem run by two lovely ladies: bara, samosas and cake.
items.value: Small Surinamese snack and cake cafe at Henck Arronstraat 8, tucked behind the Ministry of Foreign Affairs / National Assembly in the centre. Sweet and savoury Surinamese snacks, breakfast breads and cakes; a reviewer recommends bara with bakkeljauw, bokking and egg sandwich, and samosa. Weekdays only per Tripadvisor. Tripadvisor 5.0 from 1 review.
items.notes: Weekdays only, so an office-lunch option if you work nearby.
items.limits: Single source with one review (a recent listing, given its high Tripadvisor ID). No prices or exact hours.

items.label: De Patissier by X-Avenue (Ringweg-Zuid)
items.fun: Fresh cream cakes and pastries baked daily. Birthday cake shopping, sorted.
items.value: The 'sweet corner' of the X-Avenue restaurant: fresh cakes, whipped-cream pastries and savoury snacks, baked daily in its own bakery. Address Ringweg-Zuid 57, phone (+597) 8498200. Social Suriname listing updated 18 December 2025.
items.notes: Good for ordering a cake for an office birthday or your own celebration.
items.limits: One directory listing for the patisserie; Tripadvisor covers the restaurant, not the cakes. No hours, prices or reviews.

items.label: 't Vat Sidewalk Cafe (Kleine Waterstraat)
items.fun: The city's classic terrace for people-watching with a cold drink and live music.
items.value: Big open-air sidewalk cafe on Kleine Waterstraat, next to the flower market and near the riverside hotels, popular with locals and tourists for drinks, live music and snacks (satay, cassava chips, pom). Wanderlog 3.7 from 648. Reviews run to March 2026. Service is the usual complaint. Petit Bouchon bakery is upstairs.
items.notes: Sit near the service counter to get served faster. Busy, well-lit area in the evening, but take a taxi home late.
items.limits: More a bar-cafe than a coffee shop. Hours and prices not found. Street number inferred from Petit Bouchon's 'first floor of T'Vat' at Kleine Waterstraat 1.

items.label: Filipino community in Paramaribo (nurses and skilled workers)
items.fun: You are not the only Pinay here: Filipino nurses have worked in the hospitals for years.
items.value: Suriname has a small but real Filipino community. Philippine DFA releases put it at about 1,000 workers in 2014 and about 500 skilled workers in 2018, mostly in healthcare (doctors and nurses at the major hospitals since about 2013), hospitality, services, fishing, logging and engineering. In 2018 Suriname's health minister said 61 Filipino nurses worked in the country, 59 of them at the Academic Hospital Paramaribo (AZP); a later Times of Suriname article mentions 70 Filipino nurses at AZP. The community has held events such as a basketball tournament (2014) attended by the embassy. Searches found no named association, Facebook group, Filipino restaurant, Filipino-run shop or Jollibee-type outlet.
items.notes: The community seems to run on word of mouth: one kababayan nurse at AZP will probably lead you to the rest.

Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (news release)
Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (news release)

items.label: Philippine Honorary Consulate, Paramaribo (Egon Audhoe)
items.fun: Your own little slice of the Philippine government, right here in Paramaribo.
items.value: The Philippines has no embassy in Suriname; the Embassy in Brasilia covers it and runs periodic consular outreach missions in Paramaribo (a 2020 mission handled 93 services, 82 of them passport applications). Egon Audhoe was introduced to the community in 2020 as the incoming Honorary Consul and was listed as Philippine Honorary Consul in a 2022 DFA report. The official DFA directory gives the office as Laparkan Suriname NV, Nieuwe Charlesburgweg 95, Paramaribo, tel +597 8798669, supervising post Embassy of the Philippines, Brasilia. The embassy posts outreach news on Facebook (facebook.com/PHinBrazil).
items.notes: Register with the embassy and follow its Facebook page for the next outreach date; phone the consulate before going in person.

sources.publisher: Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (official directory page)
Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (news release)
Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (news release)

items.limits: Honorary consuls are part-time and not full consular posts; passports are usually handled at outreach missions or via Brasilia. Newest evidence of Audhoe in the role is 2022. No opening hours published. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.
conflicts: Address: DFA directory says Nieuwe Charlesburgweg 95 (tel +597 8798669); consulate-info.com says Henck Arronstraat 144, Centrum (tel +597 422263 / 426341, email lpksur@sr.net).

items.label: Chinese Sunday Market (Kong Ngie Tong), Van Sommelsdijckstraat
items.fun: Sunday morning steamed dumplings and pork buns: the closest thing to a merienda run.
items.value: A Sunday-only Chinese market listed as Chinese Market 广义堂星期天市场 (Kong Ngie Tong Sunday market) on Van Sommelsdijckstraat in the centre. Listings describe a bustling market with Chinese food specialties, fresh vegetables, spices and snacks; reviewers single out fresh steamed dumplings and Chinese bread filled with pork, and one calls it slightly pricey. A good place to hunt for Asian greens and noodles.
items.notes: Go early on Sunday: most of the city is closed on Sundays, so this is a lovely after-Mass outing.
items.limits: Only one listing found; exact hours, house number and whether calamansi, fish sauce or bihon are sold are not stated. Undated reviews. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Choi's Supermarket (several branches incl. Lelydorp)
items.fun: A huge everything-store: rice, sauces, snacks and probably your instant noodle fix.
items.value: Choi's describes itself as one of Suriname's leading supermarkets, founded in 1982, with over 30,000 products covering food, bakery, liquor, drugstore, household goods and produce. A Suriname travel guide calls Choi's Supermarket & Mall a one-stop shop for groceries, household goods and specialty items. A Republic Bank page lists a bank agency inside Choi's Supermarket at Indira Gandhiweg 446, Lelydorp (tel 597-471555), and Keynews reported Choi's opening a third branch in Lelydorp.
items.notes: Good for a big first stock-up of pantry basics; check the Asian aisle for soy sauce, fish sauce and rice noodles.

Republic Bank Suriname (branches and agencies page)

items.label: Tulip Supermarket
items.fun: The polished, imported-goods supermarket for when you want familiar brands.
items.value: A travel blog describes Tulip as a bona fide first-world supermarket for stocking the larder, with mostly imported stock (many American products, others from the Netherlands) and relatively high prices.
items.notes: Handy for imported comfort brands; expect to pay more than at Chinese-run shops.
items.limits: One undated blog only; no address, branch list or hours found, and nothing about its Asian range. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Chinese market on Ma Retraiteweg
items.fun: Imported Chinese goods and fresh produce: a good bet for noodles and sauces.
items.value: A Surinam Airways travel guide lists a specialty Chinese market on Ma Retraiteweg offering imported Chinese goods, fresh produce and household items.
items.notes: Take a taxi the first time and bring a photo of the labels you want (bihon, patis, Lucky Me) to show staff.
items.limits: Single source with no shop name, house number or hours; a separate search found no other page confirming it. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Fa Tai (Maagdenstraat, Spanhoek)
items.fun: Long-running Chinese spot with a dim sum reputation, right in the old centre.
items.value: Long-running Chinese restaurant at Maagdenstraat 64 in the Spanhoek area, takeaway downstairs and sit-down dining upstairs. One listing says locals recommend its dim sum and suggests weekend booking; reviewers praise tjauwmin kip and sweet and sour fish and note fairly quick service. Listed hours roughly 9:00-22:00, Monday from 10:30.
items.notes: Ask whether dim sum is on that day before you go; book at weekends.
items.limits: Dim sum claim comes from one promotional-sounding listing; no menu or prices found, Sunday hours unclear. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Liming Restaurant (Paramaribo Noord)
items.fun: Cheap daily specials and Bang Bang Fish: a solid weeknight Chinese fix.
items.value: Chinese-Surinamese restaurant in Paramaribo Noord. Reviewers recommend the tjauwmin and Bang Bang Fish, praise generous portions and budget-friendly daily specials, and mention slow service.
items.notes: Go for the meal of the day if you are watching your budget.
items.limits: Single aggregator listing; no address or hours found. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Ogi Sushi & Teppanyaki (Kleine Waterstraat)
items.fun: Teppanyaki show, cocktails and river views: birthday dinner material.
items.value: Japanese sushi and teppanyaki restaurant at Kleine Waterstraat 9 (reviewers place it in the Ramada hotel), dinner service with a river-view setting; reservations recommended. Reviewers enjoy the live teppanyaki show and cocktails; one reported food poisoning from salmon sushi and another said it is less busy than before.
items.notes: Book ahead and go with a friend for the teppanyaki show.
items.limits: Mixed, undated reviews; could not confirm still open in 2026. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Sakura Nikkei, Courtyard by Marriott
items.fun: Japanese-Peruvian fusion in a calm hotel setting, easy and safe for a solo evening.
items.value: Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian fusion) restaurant inside the Courtyard by Marriott Paramaribo, focused on fresh seafood and colourful presentation. Marriott's dining page lists it open every day 17:00-23:00.
items.notes: A hotel restaurant is a comfortable first solo dinner; taxi there and back at night.
items.limits: No menu or prices in sources; hours not dated. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: Restaurant Jawa (Kasabaholoweg)
items.fun: Some of the tastiest saoto soup in town, the warm-hug bowl you will crave.
items.value: Indonesian-Javanese restaurant at Kasabaholoweg 7, listed hours 11:00-22:00. Reviewers call it one of the best places for saoto soup and recommend Rendang Padang and dawet (iced coconut drink); prices reasonable, portions generous, service mixed.
items.notes: Saoto is the Surinamese-Javanese cousin of a comforting sabaw: perfect on a rainy day.
items.limits: Review dates unknown; no prices stated. Pages could not be opened here (network policy blocked fetching); facts come from search-result snippets of the cited URLs.

items.label: TBL Cinemas (The Back Lot Cinemas), near Hermitage Mall
items.fun: Popcorn, aircon and a big screen: the easiest solo night out in town.
items.value: TBL Cinemas, also listed as The Back Lot Cinemas, is Paramaribo's film theatre, linked to the Back Lot Foundation that runs the city's December film festival. A rental listing places it near Hermitage Mall in the south of the city, and a visitor review on Wanderlog says tickets are very cheap compared with the United States. Recent screenings listed on DutchCulture include Surinamese documentaries in 2023 and 2024. Official site: tblcinemas.com.
items.notes: Check tblcinemas.com for showtimes before you go. Pair it with dinner at Hermitage Mall and take a taxi home after late shows.
items.limits: Could not open tblcinemas.com from here, so no confirmed street address, hours or ticket price. A Numbeo-based cost page estimates an average cinema ticket at about EUR 3.93 (range EUR 3.49 to 6.12), which is only an estimate.

items.label: The Back Lot film festival at Thalia Theatre (early December)
items.fun: A week of festival films in a historic theatre, perfect for a cosy December evening.
items.value: The Back Lot Foundation, founded in 2002 by director Eddie Weingard and Hennach Dreibar, hosts an annual festival of feature and documentary films in the Thalia Theatre building in Paramaribo. Wikipedia gives the run as 6 to 11 December each year. The foundation has been supported by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Prince Claus Fund.
items.notes: Watch TBL Cinemas' and the foundation's social pages from mid-November for the 2026 programme.
items.hours: Usually 6-11 December (2026 dates not yet announced)
items.limits: Only one source (Wikipedia) for the dates and venue; no 2025 or 2026 programme was found. It may have moved to TBL Cinemas or changed dates.

items.label: Paramaribo Zoo (Rainville, next to the Cultuurtuin)
items.fun: Meet sloths, monkeys and parrots, most of them rescued Surinamese locals.
items.value: Paramaribo Zoo opened in May 1972 in Rainville, beside the Cultuurtuin. About 75 percent of the animals are native wildlife that were confiscated or were once pets, and the collection is mostly South American. Third-party listings give hours of 9:00 to 18:00 daily (another says 9:00 to 17:00) and one lists entry at SRD 15 for children aged 2 to 12 and SRD 20 for 13 and over.
items.notes: Go early in the morning before the midday heat. Bring small SRD notes.
items.limits: Hours and prices are from undated third-party listings that disagree: another says entry is free with donations, a blog says SRD 10. Prices are likely higher now given inflation. Address not confirmed.
conflicts: Closing time listed as 18:00 by one listing and 17:00 by another.
Entry listed as SRD 20 adult, as free with donations, and as SRD 10 in an older blog.

items.label: Neotropical Butterfly Park (Lelydorp)
items.fun: A garden full of fluttering blue morphos, if you phone ahead first.
items.value: The Neotropical Butterfly Park is at Lelydorperweg 127 in Lelydorp, south of Paramaribo. It has an enclosed butterfly garden, a small insect museum with Surinamese specimens and a small gallery. A traveller's blog reported entry of SRD 35 per person and an almost empty car park. a Wanderlog reviewer called it a must-visit and said staff were accommodating. Tour operators sell it as a full-day trip combined with Colakreek.
items.notes: Call ahead: WhichMuseum says it is open by appointment and also flags it as temporarily closed.
items.limits: Operating status in 2026 is unclear (listed as temporarily closed). The SRD 35 price is from an undated blog and is surely out of date.
conflicts: WhichMuseum lists it both as open by appointment and as temporarily closed.

items.label: Colakreek recreation park (Para)
items.fun: Float in cool, Coca-Cola coloured creek water under the trees.
items.value: Colakreek (Cola Creek) is a blackwater creek in Para district, about an hour from Paramaribo, named for its cola-coloured water. The resort was originally built during the Second World War for American soldiers stationed at Zanderij. Listings say weekdays are quieter than weekends, there is a cafeteria, and there is no lifeguard.
items.notes: Go on a weekday or with friends, bring your own snacks and do not swim alone, as there is no lifeguard.
items.limits: No current entry price or hours found. Check the resort's social media before going.

items.label: Fort Nieuw Amsterdam open-air museum (Commewijne)
items.fun: Cannons, river views and breezy history walks across the water.
items.value: Fort Nieuw Amsterdam was built from 1734 to 1747 where the Suriname and Commewijne rivers meet, to defend the colony. It is now an open-air museum run by the Stichting Openluchtmuseum Fort Nieuw Amsterdam, on Wilhelminastraat in Nieuw Amsterdam. TripAdvisor reviewers call it a beautiful place for a walk and suggest combining it with Mariënburg or a boat ride to Frederiksdorp.
items.notes: Bring a hat and water; it is mostly outdoors. Easy to combine with a Commewijne plantation boat tour from Leonsberg.
items.limits: No current hours or entry fee found. A post-pandemic Key News article says foreigners paid a higher tourist rate.

items.label: Mariënburg sugar plantation ruins (Commewijne)
items.fun: Rusty steam trains and old sugar factory stories told by the people who worked there.
items.value: Mariënburg was founded in 1745 and from 1882 housed a central sugar factory that produced raw sugar until the 1960s. Rusting rails, factory parts and an old steam train remain in the greenery. KLM's travel guide says elderly former employees give guided tours with old photographs, in Dutch and English. It is often part of Commewijne day tours with Peperpot and Fort Nieuw Amsterdam.
items.notes: Easiest as part of an organised Commewijne day tour with hotel pickup.
items.limits: No hours or entry fee found; the guided tours by former workers may depend on their availability.

items.label: Sunset dolphin boat tour from Leonsberg
items.fun: Watch pink-bellied river dolphins leap as the sky turns gold.
items.value: Several operators run three-hour sunset trips on the Suriname river from the Leonsberg jetty in the north of Paramaribo, leaving around 16:00 to look for Guiana dolphins. Impressive Suriname Travel lists EUR 30 per adult (EUR 25 for children 3 to 11, minimum 3 people); All Suriname Tours lists EUR 28 on a traditional tent boat; a Tourssuriname listing on Expedia shows about USD 41 with water and snacks.
items.notes: Book a few days ahead; hotel transfers are usually extra, so arrange a taxi to Leonsberg.
items.limits: Prices may have changed; minimum group sizes apply.
conflicts: Expedia price is about USD 41 versus EUR 28-30 direct.

items.label: Historical plantation boat tour in Commewijne (All Suriname Tours)
items.fun: A full day on the river: forts, plantations and maybe dolphins, lunch included.
items.value: All Suriname Tours runs a day trip from the Leonsberg jetty at 9:00, visiting Fort Nieuw Amsterdam and the Rust en Werk and Frederiksdorp plantations and returning around 15:00, with a chance to see dolphins. Listed at EUR 70 per person including transport and food, excluding alcohol.
items.notes: A good first-month Saturday outing if you want company without planning anything.
items.limits: Price from the operator's page; check current price and minimum numbers.

items.label: Sunday bird-singing contest, Onafhankelijkheidsplein
items.fun: Tiny birds, big voices, and serious men with scoreboards. Totally charming.
items.value: On Sunday mornings men gather on Independence Square with caged songbirds (twatwa, rowtie, picolet) for whistling contests, where birds earn points for their songs, tracked on a scoreboard. Travel guides say it runs from around sunrise, often 6:00 or 7:00, for a few hours.
items.notes: Go early after first Mass and bring water. Free to watch; be polite before taking photos.
items.limits: Start times vary between sources; not every Sunday may have a contest.

items.label: Numismatic Museum of the Central Bank of Suriname
items.fun: An accountant's dream: centuries of Surinamese coins and banknotes in one small room.
items.value: A small museum in the Central Bank of Suriname building at Mr. F.H.R. Lim A Postraat 7, opened in April 2002. About 60 square metres of displays cover coins and paper money from the West India Company era to today. Labels are in Dutch but audio guides are in English and Dutch. De Nederlandsche Bank has lent it five original historical artefacts.
items.notes: Phone +597 842-6640 to check opening hours before you go.
items.limits: Hours and entry fee not found; date of the DNB loan not confirmed.

items.label: Santa Rosa Church (Catholic, inner city)
items.fun: A pretty wooden Catholic church that feels a little like home.
items.value: Santa Rosa is a Roman Catholic church in central Paramaribo, inside the UNESCO World Heritage inner city. The current wooden building was consecrated on 28 June 1911, holds about 300 people and is the city's second-largest church.
items.notes: Ask the Diocese of Paramaribo (bisdomparamaribo.org) for Mass times; a good alternative to the cathedral for weekday Mass.
items.limits: No Mass schedule or language information found.

items.label: Cathedral Masses and Blessed Peerke Donders' tomb
items.fun: Pray beside a beatified missionary in the world's grandest wooden cathedral.
items.value: Blessed Peter (Peerke) Donders, the Dutch missionary who served lepers in Suriname, has been buried since 1921 in a tomb in the left wing of the Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral, renovated in 2010. A 2019 Mass listing gives weekday Masses at 6:30 and 12:00 and Sunday Masses at 19:00 (Saturday vigil) and 10:00, at Henck Arronstraat 22-24. The diocese has 31 parishes, including Heilig Hart, St Jozef (Copieweg) and Onze Lieve Vrouw van Nazareth.
items.notes: Mass is mainly in Dutch; ask at the parish office (+597 47 25 21) whether any English or youth groups meet.
items.limits: Mass times are from a 2019 listing and may have changed. No source found for an English-language Mass in Paramaribo.
conflicts: Cathedral address given as Gravenstraat 14 (GCatholic) and Henck Arronstraat 22-24 (Mass listing); the street was renamed.

items.label: Srefidensi Dey (Independence Day), 25 November 2026
items.fun: Fireworks at midnight and a parade: your first big Surinamese party, five days in.
items.value: Suriname became independent on 25 November 1975, and 25 November is a public holiday. For the 50th anniversary in 2025 the celebrations began at midnight with fireworks, followed by a military parade, wreath-layings and a reception at the Presidential Palace. 2026 is the 51st anniversary; no 2026 programme had been published when checked.
items.notes: Shops and offices close. Watch the parade near Onafhankelijkheidsplein with a colleague and keep valuables tucked away in the crowds.
items.limits: Programme details are based on 2025 (50th anniversary, larger than usual); the 2026 programme is not yet known.

items.label: Christmas tree and Enchanted Christmas Forest, Onafhankelijkheidsplein
items.fun: Fairy lights, a giant tree and free entry: Christmas magic in the tropics.
items.value: In recent years Independence Square has had a large sponsored Christmas tree lit by the president. In 2024 it hosted the free Enchanted Christmas Forest, sponsored by Big Will N.V. and open until 3 January 2025. A 2021 edition ran 17:00 to 22:00 (last entry 21:15) until 28 December.
items.notes: Go after dark on a weeknight to avoid crowds; it is right by the palace and the cathedral area.
items.hours: December to early January (2026 edition not confirmed)
items.limits: No confirmation of a 2025 or 2026 edition; it was a First Lady initiative under the previous president.

items.label: Chinese New Year, 6 February 2027
items.fun: Lion dances, drums and red lanterns to welcome the Year of the Goat.
items.value: Chinese New Year 2027 falls on Saturday 6 February and starts the Year of the Goat. Suriname's Chinese community celebrates with dragon and lion dances, often in the streets of Paramaribo, and associations hold galas: in 2026 the Suriname Chinese United Association held a gala at the Anthony Nesty Sporthal on 17 February, and Chung Fa Foei Kon held a large celebration attended by President Simons.
items.notes: Look out for announcements from Chung Fa Foei Kon and other Chinese associations in January.
items.limits: Specific 2027 events and venues are not yet announced; just after the requested window.

items.label: Riverside bar and grill (by the Waterkant)
items.fun: Simple food, cold beer and the river breeze, with karaoke if you're brave.
items.value: A popular, casual riverside bar and grill near the Waterkant. Wanderlog reviewers mention a relaxed vibe, simple tasty food, slow service and karaoke nights with locals; The Waterkant section up to the Stenen Trap reopened in November 2025 with new terraces.
items.notes: Go before dark or in a group: reviewers flag safety concerns late at night.
items.limits: No regular karaoke schedule or hours found; one review mentions hygiene concerns.

items.label: Paramaribo walking tour of the UNESCO inner city
items.fun: Learn the old wooden city's secrets in a morning, the best first-week orientation.
items.value: Guided walks of the historic inner city, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002. All Suriname Tours lists a walking tour from the Torarica hotel at EUR 25 per person. Travel The Guianas lists a UNESCO Heritage Tour at USD 45 with pickup, English-speaking guide, water and entry fees; Purity Tours on Expedia lists about USD 33 for 5 hours.
items.notes: Do this in your first week to get your bearings. Wear a hat and comfy shoes.
items.address: Starts at Torarica hotel (All Suriname Tours)
items.limits: Prices vary by operator and currency.
conflicts: Prices quoted in EUR (25) and USD (33-45) by different operators.

items.label: Cultuurtuin (Culture Garden), Rainville
items.fun: Shady paths, flowering trees and hummingbirds for a calm morning walk.
items.value: The Cultuurtuin, known locally as 'de Cul', is a large green garden just outside the centre next to the zoo. Locals walk there in groups, and birders know it for flowering trees that attract hummingbirds and honeycreepers.
items.notes: Go early morning with a walking buddy; combine with the zoo next door.
items.limits: No hours, safety or facilities information found.

items.label: Jodensavanne day trip
items.fun: Ruins of a 17th-century Jewish town in the rainforest, plus a healing spring.
items.value: Jodensavanne, on the Suriname river south of Paramaribo, has the ruins of a synagogue, a cemetery and a healing water spring. Impressive Suriname Travel runs a one-day trip by car or bus at EUR 85 per adult including lunch and entry fees, back in Paramaribo around 16:00. Longer trips combine it with Ston Island or Overbridge resort.
items.notes: A tour is the easiest way to go; bring insect repellent.
items.limits: Tour prices may change.

items.label: Braamspunt sea turtle tour (from late January)
items.fun: Watch giant leatherbacks lay eggs on a moonlit beach. Save it for the new year.
items.value: Braamspunt is a beach at the mouth of the Suriname river, reached only by boat from Leonsberg; it became a special management area in 2015. Leatherback, green and olive ridley turtles nest there. Tours leave around 17:00, include boat, guide and dinner, and cost about EUR 65 (All Suriname Tours) to USD 80. Guides use red lights only.
items.notes: Season starts about late January or February, so book for early 2027.
items.limits: Season dates differ between operators; not available Nov-Dec.
conflicts: Season given as Feb-early Aug, Mar-Aug, and end Jan-July by different sources.

items.label: Weg naar Zee (Road to the Sea)
items.fun: Drive to where the city meets the Atlantic, with temples and mangroves.
items.value: Weg naar Zee is a residential area about 15 km northwest of central Paramaribo, off Kwattaweg, with a large Hindustani community. It has an open-air crematorium (opened 1968) and a nearby Hindu pilgrimage site, and the road leads to the Atlantic shore, where there are mangrove restoration and erosion works.
items.notes: It is a muddy, mangrove coast, not a swimming beach. Go in daylight with someone who knows the area.
items.limits: No source confirms a sunset spot or beach facilities.
